questions.text: Quick Revision - Nervous System and Neuron

definitionBean.title: Nervous System and Neuron
definitionBean.definition: The system that controls all body activities and responses to the environment in organisms is called the 'nervous system', whose structural unit is the 'neuron' (nerve cell).
definitionBean.explanation: A neuron functions to transmit information from one place to another in the body in the form of electrochemical impulses.
importantPoints: Neuron (Nerve cell): Microscopic unit of the nervous system
Dendrites: The end that receives information
Axon: Long fiber structure that passes impulses forward
Synapse: Contact point between two nerve cells

questions.text: Quick Revision - Brain and Reflex Action

definitionBean.title: Human Brain and Reflex Action
definitionBean.definition: The human brain is the main organ of the central nervous system that controls thinking, vision, balance, and involuntary actions; and a sudden involuntary action in response to a stimulus is called a 'reflex action'.
definitionBean.explanation: The brain is divided into three parts - forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain (cerebellum, medulla). Reflex actions are primarily controlled by the spinal cord.
importantPoints: Forebrain: Main thinking and reasoning part
Cerebellum: Maintaining body balance and posture
Reflex Arc: Pathway of a reflex action
Medulla: Control of involuntary actions (blood pressure, salivation)

questions.text: Quick Revision - Plant and Human Hormones

definitionBean.title: Plant and Human Hormones
definitionBean.definition: Endocrine substances that establish chemical coordination in plants and animals are called 'hormones', which control growth and metabolism.
definitionBean.explanation: Plant hormones (like auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, abscisic acid) control plant growth and movement; while human hormones (like insulin, thyroxine, adrenaline) regulate various biological functions.
importantPoints: Auxin: Plant growth and bending toward light (phototropism)
Abscisic acid: Wilting of leaves and halting growth
Insulin: Controlling glucose levels in blood
Adrenaline: Hormone to face emergency situations (fight or flight)

parts.statement: Draw a labeled diagram of a neuron (nerve cell) and describe its functions.
parts.correct_answer: Neuron transmits information via electrochemical impulses.
parts.explanation: A neuron is the structural and functional unit of the nervous system. It consists of dendrites (receiving info), cell body, and axon (passing impulses forward). It transmits sensory and motor messages across the body.

parts.statement: What is a synapse? How are nerve impulses transmitted across it?
parts.correct_answer: Synapse is the gap between two neurons where chemical signals transmit impulses.
parts.explanation: The gap between two nerve cells (neurons) is called a synapse. Here, electrical impulses convert into chemical signals to cross from one neuron to the dendrite of the next.

parts.statement: What is the difference between a reflex action and walking? Explain the reflex arc.
parts.correct_answer: Reflex action is involuntary and quick, walking is voluntary.
parts.explanation: A reflex action is a sudden, involuntary, and rapid response controlled by the spinal cord, whereas walking is a voluntary action controlled by the brain. A reflex arc is the pathway through which sensory signals travel from receptors via the spinal cord to muscles.

parts.statement: Name the main parts of the human brain and state the function of the cerebellum.
parts.correct_answer: Forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain are main parts; cerebellum maintains balance.
parts.explanation: The human brain has three main parts: 1. Forebrain 2. Midbrain 3. Hindbrain. The cerebellum controls voluntary muscle movement and balance (e.g., walking straight, riding a bicycle).

parts.statement: What are plant hormones? Write the names and functions of any two plant hormones.
parts.correct_answer: Auxin (growth) and gibberellin (stem growth) are plant hormones.
parts.explanation: Plant hormones are chemical compounds that regulate growth, development, and responses to the environment in plants. Two hormones: 1. Auxin - increases cell elongation and causes bending toward light. 2. Gibberellin - helps in the growth of stems.

parts.statement: What is the role of the insulin hormone in the human body? What disease is caused by its deficiency?
parts.correct_answer: Insulin controls blood sugar, deficiency causes diabetes.
parts.explanation: The insulin hormone regulates the level of sugar (glucose) in the blood. Its deficiency increases sugar levels in the body, causing diabetes.
